🇲🇽🛡️ <u>HOMICIDES DOWN 49% — MEXICO PROVES YOU DON'T NEED MASS INCARCERATION</u>

Homicides in Mexico are down 49% under Sheinbaum — from 86.9 a day in September 2024 to 44.3.

No mano dura, no mass incarceration: 2,400 meth labs dismantled, fentanyl trafficking at the border cut sharply, and thousands of young people pulled into school and work instead of cartels. Attack the causes, not just the symptoms.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SOFT COUP IN THE GROUP STAGE — FOREIGN OPERATIVES RUN A DISINFO WAR ON MEXICO</u>

While Mexico hosts the World Cup, a foreign-run disinformation machine is working to brand it a "failed state." Contralínea names the operatives: Argentina's Fernando Cerimedo (probed by Brazil for electoral disinfo) and Spain's Javier Negre (convicted for fabricating news), pushing a soft-coup line alongside the US Embassy and the PAN.

Mexico's legal counsel laid it out publicly — right of reply, on the record.

🇲🇽🌊 <u>THE BAY IS NOT FOR SALE — MAYO-YOREME BLOCK A $1.6B AMMONIA PLANT</u>

The Mayo-Yoreme of Sinaloa are still blocking GPO's $1.6 billion ammonia plant on Ohuira Bay — a 2,220-ton-a-day facility they say threatens the mangroves, the fishing, and the people with a toxic gas leak.

Children walked the Topolobampo shoreline chanting "¡Aquí no!" Twelve years of permits, and the bay still isn't for sale.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>TENOCHTITLAN REOPENS — MEXICO WALKS BACK INTO THE TEMPLE THE EMPIRE BURIED</u>

For the first time, Mexico opens the Temple of Ehécatl and the ballcourt of Tenochtitlan to the public — sacred Mexica structures buried under the colonial capital, walkable through July 19 as part of the "Mundial Social."

INAH calls the ballcourt Teotlachco, "the game of the gods." The empire poured a cathedral on top of it; the city dug it back out.

NPR/CNBC: U.S. Pledges Generous Earthquake Relief to Venezuela
June 26, 2026 | 🟡

📰 US outlets led with Trump pledging "rapid" aid and calling Venezuelans "new and great friends" — months after US forces seized Maduro. Mexico appears once, in a list: "rescuers from multiple countries, including El Salvador, Mexico and Qatar."

🇲🇽 That one-word mention covers a 261-person Mexican brigade — 18 search dogs, 19 tons of equipment, three planeloads — among the largest foreign contingents on the ground.

• Trump: "The U.S. stands ready, willing, and able to help."
• Venezuelans are the "new and great friends" — per the government that captured their president.

CBC/YAHOO: Mexico, Canada Have Formed a Common Front on CUSMA Talks, Says Sheinbaum
June 22, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Sheinbaum says Mexico and Canada have "formed a common front" on CUSMA renewal — both backing a 16-year extension while Washington stays "more protectionist."

🇲🇽 Straight coverage: quotes Sheinbaum directly and notes Mexico has favored trilateral talks all along, while the US insists on splitting Mexico and Canada into separate bilateral tracks.

• "We have formed a common front through the communications that we have."
• "Trump...has become more protectionist. Talks are happening within this framework."

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>MORENA MOVES TO ABOLISH 'SUBSTITUTE' LEGISLATORS — IF A SEAT EMPTIES, VOTERS DECIDE</u>

Morena's Alfonso Ramírez Cuéllar is pushing a structural reform to scrap the figure of the legislative "suplente" — the unelected stand-in who inherits a deputy's or senator's seat the moment the titleholder steps aside. Under his proposal, a vacated seat would trigger a fresh election instead of an automatic handoff. "Substitutes are unnecessary," he said. "Citizens should always choose who represents them in the Chamber."

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S AVERAGE FORMAL WAGE HITS A RECORD 671 PESOS A DAY</u>

The average daily wage of IMSS-registered workers reached an all-time high of 671.3 pesos in May — up 6.6% nominal and 2.6% in real terms over the year. Since the end of the previous administration it's climbed 15.6% in real terms, from 581 to 671.3 pesos, with 22.7 million formal jobs on the books. Strip out inflation and the gain still holds — the opposite of the neoliberal decades that froze Mexican wages in place.

🇲🇽🌾 <u>1.44 BILLION PESOS FOR THE HANDS THAT FEED THE EXPORT MARKET</u>

President Sheinbaum announced 40,000 pesos each for 36,000 day-laborer families in San Quintín, Baja California — 1.44 billion pesos in total — for housing and electrification, plus a six-month drive to enroll them in IMSS social security before the export-certification deadline. These are the workers who pick produce up to 18 hours a day for US supermarkets. "Vamos a atender a todos," she said.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>PROFEPA IS SITTING ON 70 TREN MAYA ENVIRONMENTAL FILES — SOME STRETCHED TO THE 5-YEAR LIMIT</u>

A Contralínea investigation finds Mexico's environmental enforcement agency, Profepa, holding 70 open inspection files tied to the Tren Maya — 24 of them on the main rail sections — and dragging some out to the maximum five years without resolution, including damage to 8 cenotes and caves in Section 5. Profepa insists it "is not obstructing anything related to the project." The railway is running; the remediation isn't.
